newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares lost more than four percent after being hit by a soggy bullion price, depressed by reports that the Swiss bank planned to sell some of its gold reserves.
Industrials retraced earlier losses in afternoon trade after taking a beating in morning trade on weak February reserve figures and a weak Wall Street overnight.

"It has been a gloomy day all round...gold shares have taken a bit of a hiding. It is not panic selling, but shares are marked down," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
Another dealer said there were indications that central bankers in Europe were selling some of their reserves despite reports that there would be no sales this year.
Gold shares were seen looking to the bullion price for direction on Thursday. Industrials were knocked by the poor reserves figure released on Tuesday night, dealers said.
The all-share index lost 62.2 points to 7,070.4, golds ended down 60.0 points or 4.02 percent to 1,432.9 and industrials dropped 35.2 points to 8,248.8.
The trade figure was described as below expectations at a 12.5 billion rise after a loan of 2.1 billion rand. They said the figure reperesented a net fall of 1.4 billion rand from January.
Dealers said there was no panic selling, but prices were marked down. Some bottom-feeding lifted industrials and all-shares off their day lows.
The February business confidence figure, which rose to 113.2 points in February from 112.3 points the previous month, was the highest since October 1996 when it stood at 114.3.
Dealers said it did little to cheer sentiment.

The gold counters saw some heavy losses with Western Areas dropping 10.74 percent, or 650 cents to 54 rand, Vaal Reefs ditched 4.85 percent, or 16 rand to 314 rand and Freegold shed 3.58 percent, or 130 cents to 35 rand.
De Beers lost 225 cents to 154.75 rand, Engen slipped 95 cents to 24.95 rand and Nedcor bucked the trend with a 225 cent gain to 79.50 rand.
Near-dated equity futures were also weak, with industrials down on a soft Wall Street overnight and depressed by disappointing reserve figures. Gold contracts slipped on the soft bullion price.
The March all-share contract was last at 6,415/25 from 6,503, the industrial contract was at 7,935/44 from 7,976 and the gold contract was at 985/1,000 from 1,059.
